evidence.quote: The Byway passes through a series of distinct rural landscapes including railroad stations, small rural communities, an unforgettable two mile road section canopied by trees and shouldered by historic dry-laid limestone fences

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration recognizes this National Scenic Byway for a landscape where diversified farming and the international equine industry coexist.
evidence.quote: Here, traditional diversified agriculture and the international equine industry thrive and coexist in a unique landscape

evidence.quote: Old Frankfort Pike Historic and Scenic Byway National Scenic Byway

evidence.claim: The local byway organization gives a nonstop drive from US 60 to the viewing area near Lexington about half an hour.
evidence.quote: Travelers can make a leisurely, non-stop drive along Old Frankfort Pike from US 60 near Frankfort to the Visitor Viewing Area near Lexington (or vice-versa) in about ½ hour.

evidence.claim: Under the rolling plain lies phosphate-rich limestone, with springs that flow for miles before sinking underground or disappearing into caves.
evidence.quote: The region is a gently rolling plain of deep loam soils atop phosphate-rich limestone; wild with springs that flow for miles only to sink underground or disappear into caves.

evidence.claim: This stretch of KY 1681 belonged to the original road between Frankfort and Lexington.
evidence.quote: This stretch of road was part of the original thoroughfare between Frankfort and Lexington.

evidence.claim: In 1988, the Lexington-Frankfort Scenic Corridor organization formed to preserve and conserve the surrounding area.
evidence.quote: It was formed in 1988 to advance the preservation, conservation, and enhancement of this area known as the Lexington-Frankfort Scenic Corridor.

evidence.claim: It later sponsored the national byway nomination, and the road received that designation in 2021.
evidence.quote: undertook sponsorship of the National Scenic Byway nomination.

evidence.claim: the road received that designation in 2021.
evidence.quote: Old Frankfort Pike was designated a National Scenic Byway in 2021.

evidence.claim: The designated 15.5 miles pass through six National Register rural historic districts.
evidence.quote: The 15.5 miles of designated byway features a canopy of hardwood trees, miles of dry-laid limestone rock fences, and passes through six designated National Register of Historic Places Rural Historic Districts.

evidence.claim: Drive east from Duckers Station Road in Woodford County toward Wolf Run Creek at Lexington’s edge.
evidence.quote: The designated portion of the Scenic Byway extends from the west at Duckers Station Road in Woodford County to east at Wolf Run Creek in Fayette County just outside of Lexington.

evidence.claim: KY 1681 passes the former Woodburn Stud, now operated as Airdrie Stud.
evidence.quote: The route passes the site of Woodburn Stud, the birthplace of Kentucky's thoroughbred industry. The farm is now operated under the name Airdrie Stud.

evidence.claim: Midway Road has the route’s four-way stop.
evidence.quote: There is one four-way stop at the intersection of Midway Road

evidence.claim: Near the eastern end, the viewing area at Alexandria Drive explains the pike’s history.
evidence.quote: Near the east end of the byway, read about the history of the Pike and the surrounding neighborhood along the self-guided walking loop at the Old Frankfort Pike Visitor Viewing Area at the roundabout intersection of the Pike and Alexandria Drive.

evidence.claim: Off the pike, McConnell Springs adds a separate excursion to the encampment where Lexington was named.
evidence.quote: Finally, the McConnell Springs Visitor Center and Nature Sanctuary marks the original 1775 encampment where Lexington was named. This city park located off Old Frankfort Pike

evidence.claim: Dry-laid limestone fences border the two-mile stretch beneath the trees.
evidence.quote: an unforgettable two mile road section canopied by trees and shouldered by historic dry-laid limestone fences

evidence.claim: Woodburn’s horse-breeding history includes a break for cattle.
evidence.quote: Not long into the 20th century, the farm was no longer in the horse business and had been converted to cattle land.

evidence.claim: During the nineteenth century, the farm was home to Lexington, America’s leading sire for sixteen years.
evidence.quote: Woodburn Stud was home to the stallion Lexington (1850–1875), America's leading sire for sixteen years.

evidence.claim: His offspring included Preakness, the horse whose name became that of the Preakness Stakes.
evidence.quote: Lexington sired numerous champions and winners of major races including Duke of Magenta, Kentucky and Preakness, for whom the Preakness Stakes is named.

evidence.claim: Woodburn also bred Standardbreds for harness racing and was best known for these trotting horses during the middle and later nineteenth century.
evidence.quote: in fact during the mid- to late 19th century, Woodburn was where the Standardbred horse originated and the farm was best known for these trotting horses for harness racing.

evidence.claim: After A. J. Alexander died in 1902, the operation declined and the land shifted to cattle.
evidence.quote: But after A.J.'s death in 1902, it went into decline. Not long into the 20th century, the farm was no longer in the horse business and had been converted to cattle land.

evidence.claim: Horse breeding returned in 1972 under the Airdrie Stud name, on land that includes much of the former Woodburn property.
evidence.quote: the horse breeding business was revived in 1972 as Airdrie Stud Inc. which now operates on 2,500 acres (10 km2), much of which is part of the original Woodburn Stud lands.

evidence.claim: A bronze Secretariat stretches across the roundabout at Alexandria Drive.
evidence.quote: At the intersection of the Pike and Alexandria Road, the larger-than-life bronze statue of "Secretariat" stretches across the roundabout.

evidence.claim: The viewing area sits to its southeast, with a brick-paved loop and interpretive panels on the pike and the wider Lexington-Frankfort Scenic Corridor.
evidence.quote: It contains vehicle parking, a brick paved loop trail, and a number of interpretive panels that tell the many stories of Old Frankfort Pike and the greater Lexington-Frankfort Scenic Corridor.

evidence.claim: The viewing area sits to its southeast,
evidence.quote: located at the southeast corner of the roundabout at Old Frankfort Pike and Alexandria Drive.

evidence.claim: The statue is visible from the viewing area.
evidence.quote: From this vantage, the statue of SECRETARIAT is visible at the center of the roundabout.

evidence.claim: This is the Lexington end of a road recognized as a Kentucky Scenic Byway since the 1990s and a National Scenic Byway since February 2021.
evidence.quote: The Pike was designated a NATIONAL SCENIC BYWAY in February, 2021. The road has been a KENTUCKY SCENIC BYWAY since the 1990s

evidence.claim: This is the Lexington end
evidence.quote: Visit the Visitor Viewing Area at the Lexington end of the Pike.

evidence.claim: Secretariat’s bronze figure occupies the roundabout, visible from the viewing area.
evidence.quote: From this vantage, the statue of SECRETARIAT is visible at the center of the roundabout.

evidence.claim: At McConnell Springs, water appears above ground, disappears and returns, finally surfacing again a third of a mile away.
evidence.quote: a series of artesian springs that come to the surface, go underground, reappear, flow on the surface and go back underground only to surface again a third of a mile away.

evidence.claim: The limestone landscape contains sinkholes, underground streams and springs formed as water dissolves soluble rock.
evidence.quote: This type of landscape is the result of water dissolving soluble rock, such as limestone, thus creating sinkholes, underground streams, caves, and springs.

evidence.claim: William McConnell’s party camped here in June 1775 and named the camp Lexington in honor of the Revolutionary War battle in Massachusetts.
evidence.quote: William McConnell and his party of kinsmen, companion surveyors, explorers and would-be settlers established a small camp in this area in June 1775. The group named their camp "Lexington" in honor of one of the first battles of the American Revolutionary War in Lexington, Massachusetts.

evidence.claim: Later uses left stone fences, a barn foundation and a small quarry visible in the park.
evidence.quote: remnants of past use still visible throughout the park - including stone fences, a barn foundation, a small rock quarry

evidence.claim: The park opened to the public in 1994 after debris removal and restoration work.
evidence.quote: Debris was removed from the site, and the land was placed into the city park system to be preserved. The Kentucky American Water Nature Center was constructed, and the park was opened to the public in 1994.

evidence.claim: The Blue Hole spring’s blue appearance comes from its fifteen-foot depth.
evidence.quote: The first is The Blue Hole, which gets its name due to appearance of the water looking blue. The illusion of the colored water is due to the 15 foot depth of this spring.

flags: The national designation covers 15.5 miles, not the full 19-mile mapped corridor or the full length of KY 1681. The drive-time estimate applies to US 60 through the visitor viewing area.
No current claims were dropped for lack of cache support. Woodburn is treated as a roadside historic farm subject, without implying public admission.
Viewing-area moment is shorter than 90 words because the cache supports only a compact account of the statue, loop and panels; additional logistics would pad the story.
